answer: A public fraud-bounty bond makes each identity expensive to fake: to register, an agent locks a deposit and publishes a cipher commitment to its credentials, like a carved timber seal no one else can copy. If anyone proves the same person controls two identities, the bond is slashed and part of it pays the whistleblower as a jade reward. Creating a hundred sock puppets then costs a hundred bonds, while honest agents risk nothing. Its limit is detection: the bounty only works if duplicates can actually be proven, so it pairs best with independent checks rather than standing alone.
